title: AdicPurityFiniteTensor
statement: Using the root quotient maps [def-pur-adic-root-comparisons], define finite tensor by the actual Tate line. It is additive and exact when the coefficient prime is invertible. Define the unique ordinary integral-twist/restriction comparison which sends each local balanced tensor $x\otimes y$ to $x\otimes c_d(y)$. Define the unique comparison of fixed and intrinsic finite tensor realizations which carries every scalar-unit pure tensor to that same pure tensor. These equations hold for every module and every test object.

proof.text: For the ordinary restriction comparison, choose the normalized component supplied by lem-pur-adic-twist-restriction-components for each module. Prove naturality on local pure tensors using the map formula for site tensor. The tensor/sheafification adjunction makes pure tensors jointly determining, proving naturality and uniqueness of the resulting natural isomorphism.

proof.text: Specialize coefficientTwistLine_exact to the finite first root line and the nonnegative exponent d. Its existing rank-one instance supplies additivity and preservation of finite limits and colimits.

proof.text: For finite realization, use the normalized objectwise isomorphism of lem-pur-adic-finite-tensor-components. The realization unit is surjective on each section: after forgetting modules it is sheafification of an already sheaf-valued presheaf. Thus scalar-unit pure tensors determine every component. On these tensors naturality is naturality of the realization unit and the lax tensor map of sheaf inclusion. Tensor extensionality proves the naturality square and uniqueness.
